key_insight: GaMO uses geometry-aware, multi-view diffusion outpainting to synthesize novel, multi-view-consistent images from few input views, enabling markedly better 3D reconstruction under sparse-view capture.
problem_solved: Poor 3D reconstruction quality when input views are limited — existing regularizers, semantic priors, or naive novel-view synthesis fail to produce geometry-consistent augmentations for downstream reconstruction.
method: Multi-view diffusion outpainting: generate novel views conditioned on sparse RGB inputs and target camera poses to densify the view set.
Geometry-aware conditioning: incorporate pose, depth/epipolar constraints and multi-view consistency into the diffusion process to ensure synthesized images are geometrically plausible.
Data augmentation for reconstruction: use synthesized multi-view-consistent images to train or fine-tune 3D reconstruction pipelines, improving fidelity from sparse captures.
impact: Reduces the number of required captures and boosts 3D reconstruction quality in low-data scenarios, making realistic scene capture more practical for researchers and practitioners working with limited viewpoints.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse input views -> geometry-aware diffusion outpainting -> augmented dense views -> 3D reconstruction output
Before/after comparison: reconstruction from sparse views vs. reconstruction using GaMO-augmented views (side-by-side renderings)
Architecture block: diffusion module + geometry-conditioning (pose/depth/epipolar) with arrows showing information flow
Performance chart: reconstruction metric improvements (e.g., IoU/Chamfer/PSNR) vs. number of input views
paper_title: GaMO: Geometry-aware Multi-view Diffusion Outpainting for Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Yi-Chuan Huang, Hao-Jen Chien, Chin-Yang Lin, Ying-Huan Chen, Yu-Lun Liu
